lint_etiquette.assessment: Lint was treated constructively. Approximately 18 displayed E-class lint firings occurred, chiefly covered-content collisions, and warnings included unreadable labels, clipped text, and co-linear edges. All were resolved before commit, as shown by the final clean diagnostics. Several issues took multiple turns, but the agent changed tactics through anchor changes, label movement, text shortening, resizing, and rerouting; no identical lint was re-fired for more than three consecutive turns without a strategy change. No warning was silently overridden or committed open, so no warning-override reason was required in the summary.

economy.assessment: The session used 130 tool calls to produce 70 committed patch operations for a large, multi-region architecture diagram. The call count is substantial and many objects were placed and labeled in separate calls, but it remained proportionate to the unusually detailed ask. There were no add-delete-rebuild cycles, repeated NO-OPs, or abandonment. Label and route corrections were somewhat lengthy but were directed responses to changing lint and did not constitute destructive thrash. Wall time was 897 seconds (14.95 minutes), narrowly within the 15-minute budget, and finalize was reached well below the 300-turn ceiling.
